domain_label: Plated-Jewelry Finishes — FTC Gold Systems, Rhodium-over-Silver Science & Thickness-Durability Engineering
purpose: A method for specifying and honestly labelling plated-jewelry finish systems — gold electroplate / vermeil / gold-filled under the exact FTC 16 CFR Part 23 thresholds [FACT], and rhodium plating over sterling silver and white gold with the correct tarnish/PGM science [FACT] — by fixing each finish's karat, thickness class, barrier/strike stack, nickel-release compliance and topcoat, so a fashion-jewelry SKU aimed at 18-25 skin-contact wear can be built to a durability gate and priced without ever inventing a market share, a demographic rate, or a durability claim the tests have not earned.
assumptions: the US FTC Jewelry Guides (16 CFR Part 23) definitions are cited public facts: sterling silver = 92.5% Ag [FACT]; gold electroplate = >=0.175 micron (7 millionths inch) of >=10k fine gold by an electrolytic process [FACT]; gold flash/wash = under 0.175 micron [FACT]; vermeil = a base of sterling silver coated with gold (or gold alloy) of at least 10 karat and at least 2.5 microns thick [FACT]; gold-filled = a karat-gold layer mechanically bonded to a base at >=1/20 (5%) of total weight, rolled-gold-plate below that fraction [FACT]

silver tarnish is a real chemical reaction, not a folk 'un-shining': metallic Ag reacts with sulfur species (H2S, carbonyl sulfide, sulfur in rubber/wool/foods) to form black silver sulfide Ag2S (and AgCl in chloride), while gold is noble and does not tarnish [FACT]; rhodium, a platinum-group metal that is hard, bright bluish-white, highly reflective and chemically inert, is electroplated as a thin barrier that both prevents the sulfur reaching the silver and supplies the bright-white cosmetic finish [FACT]

the owner's rough model ('rhodium is used on silver to make it shiny and keep it shiny / prevent unshine') is directionally right and is sharpened here into the exact Ag2S + PGM-barrier mechanism; this KB carries the corrected science as the anchor [FACT]

plating-thickness-vs-durability CLASS STRUCTURE is a published fact (flash < 0.175 um, gold-plate ~0.5 um, micron plating ~1 um, heavy/hard-wear 2.5-5 um; rhodium flash ~0.05-0.1 um, standard ~0.1-0.25 um) but the exact wear life of a given SKU in real wear is an [ESTIMATE] gated by durability tests, never a measured guarantee

EN 1811 nickel-release (0.5 ug/cm2/week for prolonged-contact articles, 0.2 for piercing posts; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 27) is a cited regulatory fact that binds nickel-barrier choices for 18-25 skin-contact wear [FACT]

no market number is invented: any 'what % is gold-plated vs solid', 'which finish sells', 'how many buy which' is encoded as a [METHOD] to measure it or an honest [UNKNOWN]; every non-fact is tagged [ESTIMATE] (method+confidence) or [UNKNOWN]; only materials-science and regulatory facts are tagged [FACT] with basis
exclusions: base-metal substrate selection (brass, 316L, copper, zinc, sterling as a base body) — that is kb1_substrates_base_metals; this KB takes the substrate as given and specifies the finish ON it

the full quality-grading test batteries and the cost-vs-quality tradeoff curve and batch economics — that is kb3_quality_cost_value_engineering; this KB defines the finish and its acceptance gate but does not build the cost curve

the bath chemistry, cell design and continuous-line process detail (cyanide vs sulfite gold, e-coat cell voltages, PVD plasma parameters) — those live in analysis/taxonomy and processes/*.json and are referenced, not re-derived

consumer demographics, category demand sizing, brand mapping and price-tier structure — those are the S1 market specialist's KBs; this KB supplies only the finish-share MEASUREMENT METHOD, never the shares
asserting any actual market share, demographic purchase rate, competitor finish mix, or retail price as measured fact

competency_questions.question: What are the exact FTC 16 CFR Part 23 thresholds that separate gold flash, gold electroplate, vermeil and gold-filled, and why can a finish only carry each name if it meets them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FTC_JEWELRY_GUIDES states 16 CFR Part 23 as the frame; GOLD_PLATED_DEFINITION gives >=0.175 um / >=10k electroplate with flash under 0.175; VERMEIL_DEFINITION gives >=2.5 um of >=10k gold over a sterling (92.5% Ag) base; GOLD_FILLED_DEFINITION gives the mechanically-bonded >=1/20-by-weight karat layer, all as [FACT] with basis

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FINISH_SPEC_HANDOFF delivers per-SKU finish system + karat + thickness class + barrier + skin-safety + label + honesty ledger, and explicitly stops before the cost curve and the demand read

competency_questions.question: What is the karat/fineness basis, and how do sterling and gold purity feed every finish definition?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: KARAT_FINENESS_BASIS states karat (x/24) and millesimal fineness, sterling = 925, and the >=10k floor the gold finishes reference [FACT]

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DURABILITY_ACCEPTANCE_TESTS names adhesion, porosity, tarnish/salt-spray, wear/abrasion and (EU) nickel-release-after-wear tests as the gate that converts an [ESTIMATE] wear life into an evidenced claim

glossary.definition: The US Federal Trade Commission Guides for the Jewelry, Precious Metals and Pewter Industries that define how finish/quality terms may be used: they fix 'gold electroplate', 'gold flash/wash', 'gold-filled', 'rolled gold plate', 'vermeil', 'rhodium' and 'sterling silver', and make an unqualified name a misrepresentation if the article does not meet the stated karat/thickness/bonding thresholds [FACT-FTC].

Per FTC 16 CFR 23: a base of STERLING SILVER coated with gold (or gold alloy) of at least 10 karat and a minimum 2.5 microns (100 millionths inch) thickness; gold over any non-sterling base, or thinner/lower-karat gold over sterling, is NOT vermeil and may not be so labelled [FACT-FTC].

FTC: 'gold electroplate' = an electrolytically deposited layer of >=10k fine gold at least 0.175 micron (7 millionths inch) thick; below 0.175 micron it is 'gold flash' or 'gold wash' and cannot be called plate; 'heavy gold electroplate' requires >=2.5 micron [FACT-FTC].

FTC: a karat-gold layer MECHANICALLY bonded (heat+pressure, not electroplated) to a base metal; 'gold-filled' requires the gold layer to be at least 1/20 (5%) of the article's total weight (of stated karat, e.g. 14k), 'rolled gold plate' (RGP) for lesser fractions which must be marked with the fraction and karat [FACT-FTC]; far more gold than electroplate, and durable, but not solid gold.

An alloy of at least 92.5% silver by weight (the balance usually copper); the base body for vermeil and the classic rhodium-plated substrate; the copper and the silver both drive tarnish, which is why sterling is often rhodium-plated or anti-tarnish-treated [FACT].

The black corrosion film on silver: metallic Ag reacts with atmospheric/contact sulfur (H2S, carbonyl sulfide, sulfur in rubber, wool, eggs) to form Ag2S (and AgCl with chloride) — a real chemical reaction, not a loss of polish; gold and rhodium, being noble/inert, do not undergo it [FACT].

A platinum-group metal, atomic number 45; hard (~800-1000 HV, far harder than gold's 60-90), bright bluish-white, highly reflective and chemically inert; electroplated in thin layers (rhodium baths are sulfate/phosphate acid systems) as the bright-white, tarnish-resistant top finish on sterling silver and white gold [FACT].

An underplate between base metal and the noble top layer: a 'strike' is a thin high-adhesion first deposit (e.g. Wood's nickel strike, gold strike); a diffusion barrier (nickel, or nickel-free palladium / Pd-Ni) blocks base-metal atoms (Cu, Fe, Ag) migrating through porous gold/rhodium and creeping tarnish/discolouration to the surface [FACT-mechanism].

The EU test method (bound by REACH Annex XVII entry 27) capping nickel release from skin-contact items at 0.5 ug/cm2/week for prolonged-contact articles and 0.2 for piercing posts, measured after simulated wear+corrosion (EN 12472); the compliance gate for a nickel-barrier or nickel-hardened finish on 18-25 skin-contact jewelry [FACT-regulation].

The trade/standard ladder relating deposited thickness to wear life: gold flash <0.175 um (decorative, wears fast), 'gold plated' ~0.5 um, micron plating ~1 um, heavy/hard-wear 2.5-5 um; rhodium flash ~0.05-0.1 um vs standard ~0.1-0.25 um; the class is [FACT] but the real-wear life of a given SKU is an [ESTIMATE] gated by tests [FACT class / ESTIMATE life].

A post-plate protective layer: a self-limiting electrophoretic clear lacquer (5-25 um) or a molecular benzotriazole/thiol anti-tarnish film that seals pores and lets an economically thin gold layer wear like a thicker one; it is a durability aid, NOT a legal substitute for the karat/thickness/nickel-release stack [FACT-practice].

A dry vacuum-deposited decorative finish: a hard nitride color layer (TiN/ZrN gold-tone, ~1500-2500 HV) often capped with a thin real-gold flash ('ion-plated gold'); far more scratch-resistant than electroplated gold, but a 'gold plated' marketing claim still requires real gold at the surface per the marking guides [FACT].

nodes.definition: Establish the regulatory frame that governs every finish name in this KB: the US FTC Guides for the Jewelry, Precious Metals and Pewter Industries, 16 CFR Part 23 [FACT-FTC]. The guides make it a deceptive act to call an article 'gold', 'gold-plated', 'gold-filled', 'vermeil', 'rhodium' or 'sterling' unless it meets the stated karat, thickness or bonding threshold, and require disclosure/qualification (e.g. the karat and fraction on rolled-gold-plate, 'plated' where a coating is thin). This node fixes the vocabulary and the honesty rule the whole finish stack is written against; the exact numeric thresholds are stated in the dependent definition nodes. It is a [FACT] anchor (public regulation), not a market claim, and it is the reason 'label it honestly' is a hard constraint rather than a preference.

the deception/qualification rule
the vocabulary the definition nodes fill in

assuming the US guides cover hallmarking obligations in other markets

nodes.definition: Fix the correct science the owner's 'keep silver shiny / prevent unshine' intuition points at: silver tarnish is a chemical reaction, not a loss of polish. Metallic silver reacts with sulfur species in air and contact — hydrogen sulfide (H2S), carbonyl sulfide, and sulfur in rubber, wool, eggs, some cosmetics — to form black silver sulfide, Ag2S (and silver chloride AgCl where chloride/sweat is present) [FACT]. The reaction proceeds even at trace ppb sulfur; copper in sterling (7.5%) adds its own oxide/sulfide darkening. Gold is noble and does not tarnish; rhodium (an inert PGM) does not either — which is exactly why a barrier of one of them over silver both stops the sulfur reaching the Ag and removes the tarnish problem. This node is the mechanistic basis every rhodium-over-silver and anti-tarnish-topcoat decision rests on [FACT].

included: Ag + sulfur -> Ag2S (and AgCl) tarnish reaction
the sulfur sources and copper contribution
gold/rhodium nobility as the reason a barrier works

pros.claim: Stating the Ag2S mechanism replaces a vague folk model with the exact reaction, so every anti-tarnish choice is reasoned not guessed
pros.example: knowing sulfur is the driver explains why a rubber band or wool box blackens silver while a sealed anti-tarnish bag does not

cons.claim: The chemistry alone does not tell you how thick a barrier must be to stop it, which needs the thickness/porosity nodes
cons.example: a porous 0.05 um layer still lets sulfur through at pinholes despite the correct mechanism

failure_modes: describing tarnish as 'the shine wearing off' and mis-prescribing polishing instead of a barrier
ignoring that porous thin noble layers still allow sulfur ingress at pores
acceptance_tests: the Ag + sulfur -> Ag2S (black silver sulfide) reaction, its sulfur sources, the AgCl/chloride variant and gold/rhodium nobility are stated as the [FACT] tarnish basis
revisit_triggers: a new anti-tarnish claim needs its mechanism checked against Ag2S chemistry
a substrate change alters the tarnishing metal
field returns show tarnish despite a barrier (porosity investigation)

base.update_signal: a tarnish field failure or a new anti-tarnish mechanism claim

nodes.definition: State what rhodium actually is, because it is the KB's central material: rhodium (Rh, atomic number 45) is a platinum-group metal that is hard (~800-1000 HV, an order of magnitude harder than soft gold's ~60-90 HV), bright bluish-white, highly reflective, and chemically inert (it resists tarnish, most acids and oxidation at room temperature) [FACT]. It is also expensive and volatile in price (a thin-film precious metal). These four properties — hardness, bright-white colour, high reflectivity, inertness — are jointly why rhodium is electroplated as a thin top finish: it supplies the mirror-white cosmetic AND a hard, non-reactive barrier in one layer. This node is the property basis that RHODIUM_OVER_SILVER, WHITE_GOLD_RHODIUM and RHODIUM_THICKNESS_DURABILITY all draw on [FACT].

included: rhodium as a hard, bright-white, reflective, inert PGM
the price/volatility caveat
the property basis for using it as a thin top finish

pros.claim: Naming rhodium's four load-bearing properties explains in one place why it is both the colour and the protection
pros.example: its inertness gives tarnish resistance while its reflectivity gives the mirror-white look, so one dip does two jobs

cons.claim: Rhodium's cost and price volatility make thickness a real economic lever, so the property view must not imply 'more is always better'
cons.example: a thick rhodium layer is brittle and costly, so the property advantage is bounded by thickness economics

failure_modes: treating rhodium as 'white gold' or a gold substitute rather than a distinct PGM
implying unlimited thickness because the properties are good, ignoring cost/brittleness
acceptance_tests: rhodium is stated as a hard (~800-1000 HV), bright bluish-white, highly reflective, chemically inert PGM with a price-volatility caveat, tagged [FACT]
revisit_triggers: a rhodium price spike changes the thickness economics
a substitute white PGM (ruthenium, palladium-white) is evaluated
a supplier bath change alters the achievable colour/hardness

base.update_signal: a rhodium price move or a white-PGM substitute evaluation

nodes.definition: Fix the purity vocabulary every gold and silver finish threshold references: karat expresses gold content as parts-in-24 (24k = pure, 18k = 75.0%, 14k = 58.3%, 10k = 41.7% — the FTC floor for calling something 'gold' in the US), and millesimal fineness expresses it in parts-per-thousand (750, 585, 417). Silver is expressed in fineness too: sterling = 925 (92.5% Ag), fine = 999 [FACT]. Gold plating deposits are near-pure (23.5-24k / 995-999 fine) unless hardened. This node exists so that 'at least 10k' in the electroplate/vermeil definitions and '92.5% Ag' in the sterling base both trace to one purity basis; it is a [FACT] scaffold, not a market or cost claim.

included: karat as x/24, millesimal fineness, the 10k gold floor
sterling = 925 and fine = 999
near-pure plated-gold purity

pros.claim: One purity basis lets every threshold ('>=10k', '925') be read consistently instead of re-explained per finish
pros.example: the vermeil '>=10k' and the electroplate '>=10k' floors both resolve to 41.7% via this node

cons.claim: Purity alone says nothing about thickness or wear, so it must always be paired with a thickness class
cons.example: a 24k flash and a 24k micron plate are equally pure but wildly different in durability

failure_modes: conflating high karat with high durability
mixing karat and fineness numbers when comparing finishes
acceptance_tests: karat as x/24 with the 10k floor, millesimal fineness, sterling = 925 and fine = 999 are stated as the [FACT] purity basis
revisit_triggers: a market uses a different legal minimum karat
a hardened-gold alloy shifts the deposit purity
a fineness-marking requirement changes

base.update_signal: a legal minimum-karat or fineness-marking change

nodes.definition: State the FTC electroplate thresholds precisely: 'gold electroplate' = an electrolytically deposited layer of at least 10k fine gold at least 0.175 micron (7 millionths of an inch) thick; below 0.175 micron the coating is 'gold flash' or 'gold wash' and may NOT be called plate; 'heavy gold electroplate' requires at least 2.5 microns [FACT-FTC]. This is the owner's core 'gold-plated' category. It matters commercially because most fashion jewelry lives here, and because the 0.175 um line is a legal naming boundary, not a quality opinion. Purity references KARAT_FINENESS_BASIS (>=10k) and the frame references FTC_JEWELRY_GUIDES. Thin flash is legitimate for low-wear decorative pieces but is where 'wears off in weeks' complaints originate when it is oversold.

included: electroplate >=0.175 um / >=10k
flash/wash under 0.175 um
heavy electroplate >=2.5 um

pros.claim: Fixing the 0.175 um plate/flash line gives an unambiguous, legally grounded name for the owner's main category
pros.example: a 0.1 um coating must be sold as 'gold flash', not 'gold plated', which pre-empts a mislabel complaint

cons.claim: The thickness threshold names the finish but does not guarantee wear life, which depends on barrier, porosity and topcoat
cons.example: a compliant 0.2 um plate over a poor barrier can still corrode at pores despite meeting the name

failure_modes: calling a sub-0.175 um flash 'gold plated'
assuming meeting the plate thickness guarantees durability without a barrier
acceptance_tests: gold electroplate >=0.175 um / >=10k, flash/wash under 0.175 um, and heavy electroplate >=2.5 um are stated as [FACT-FTC] thresholds
revisit_triggers: the FTC revises the electroplate thickness thresholds
a SKU's measured thickness crosses the flash/plate line
a market requires a different plate-naming rule

base.update_signal: an FTC electroplate threshold change or a SKU crossing the flash/plate line

nodes.definition: State the vermeil rule exactly, because it is the most-abused term in fashion jewelry: FTC 16 CFR 23 defines vermeil as a base of STERLING SILVER coated with gold (or gold alloy) of at least 10 karat and a minimum thickness throughout equivalent to 2.5 microns (100 millionths of an inch) of fine gold [FACT-FTC]. All three conditions bind: sterling base (not brass), >=10k gold, >=2.5 um. Gold over brass at 2.5 um is NOT vermeil (wrong base); gold flash over sterling is NOT vermeil (too thin). Vermeil is the premium plated tier — real precious-metal base plus a heavy gold layer — and it commands a higher price precisely because it is defined and defensible. This node depends on the electroplate node (it is the sterling-base, heavy-thickness variant) and on the purity basis.

included: the three binding vermeil conditions (sterling base, >=10k, >=2.5 um)
the non-vermeil counterexamples
vermeil as the premium plated tier
excluded: rhodium over the same sterling base (RHODIUM_OVER_SILVER)

pros.claim: Pinning all three conditions stops the common mislabel of thin or brass-based gold as vermeil
pros.example: 2.5 um gold over brass is disqualified as vermeil for the base alone, protecting the price-defensible label

cons.claim: The sterling base makes vermeil costlier than brass-based plate, so the premium label carries a real COGS
cons.example: choosing vermeil over gold-plated-brass raises material cost even before the heavier gold layer

failure_modes: labelling gold-over-brass as vermeil
labelling sub-2.5 um gold-over-sterling as vermeil
acceptance_tests: vermeil is stated as sterling base + >=10k gold + >=2.5 um, with the brass-base and thin-gold disqualifiers, tagged [FACT-FTC]
revisit_triggers: the FTC revises the vermeil definition
a SKU's base or gold thickness fails a vermeil condition
a market defines vermeil differently

base.update_signal: an FTC vermeil revision or a SKU failing a vermeil condition

nodes.definition: State the gold-filled rule, which is categorically different from electroplate: FTC defines 'gold-filled' as a layer of karat gold MECHANICALLY bonded (by heat and pressure, not electrodeposition) to a base metal, where the gold layer is at least 1/20 (5%) of the article's total weight, marked with the karat (e.g. '14k gold-filled' or '1/20 14k GF'); a lesser fraction is 'rolled gold plate' (RGP) and must be marked with its fraction and karat [FACT-FTC]. Gold-filled carries roughly 50-100x the gold of typical electroplate and wears for decades, but it is bonded sheet, not solid gold, and not plating — so it belongs in the finish vocabulary as the durable, higher-gold alternative to electroplate/vermeil. This node depends on the FTC frame and the purity basis and is kept distinct so category counts and labels do not blur plated with filled.

included: mechanically-bonded karat layer >=1/20 by weight
rolled gold plate for lesser fractions and its marking
gold-filled as the high-gold durable alternative

pros.claim: Separating gold-filled from electroplate prevents blurring a decades-durable bonded layer with a thin electro-deposit
pros.example: counting '14k gold-filled' pieces as 'gold-plated' would badly mis-state both durability and gold content

cons.claim: Gold-filled is a different manufacturing route (bonded sheet) the owner's plating line may not produce, so it is a sourcing decision not just a finish
cons.example: making gold-filled needs mill-bonded stock, not the electroplating cell

failure_modes: labelling electroplate as gold-filled or vice versa
omitting the required fraction+karat mark on rolled gold plate
acceptance_tests: gold-filled = mechanically-bonded karat layer >=1/20 by weight (marked karat), with rolled gold plate for lesser fractions, stated as [FACT-FTC]
revisit_triggers: the FTC revises the gold-filled/RGP fractions or marking
the owner considers sourcing gold-filled stock
a category count risks blurring filled with plated

base.update_signal: an FTC gold-filled/RGP revision or a gold-filled sourcing decision

nodes.definition: Describe the gold-deposit engineering that sets colour and wear: pure electroplated gold is soft (~60-90 HV) and bright but smears and wears through on high-touch items; 'hard gold' co-deposits ~0.1-0.5 wt% cobalt or nickel to refine grain and reach ~130-200 HV, the wear grade used on rings and connectors [FACT, from the electroplating source]. Colour is tuned by hardener and alloy: Co-hardened runs rich yellow to slight rose (Swiss/NIHS 1N-2N tones), Ni-hardened runs paler/greener; dedicated alloy baths give rose (Au-Cu) and green (Au-Ag) golds; 24k reads deep yellow, 18k-look and 14k-look hues are matched by alloy. The catch: hard gold is brittle (elongation well under ~1%), so a hard-gold-plated wire cracks if formed AFTER plating — form first, then plate. Ni-hardened gold also puts nickel in the surface layer itself, which conflicts with hypoallergenic claims. This node feeds the durability and PVD-comparator nodes.

included: soft vs Co/Ni-hardened gold hardness
colour tones (1N-2N, rose, green) by hardener/alloy
hard-gold brittleness and the Ni-in-surface hypoallergenic catch

pros.claim: Separating colour and hardness levers lets a SKU hit both a target tone and a wear grade deliberately
pros.example: a ring wear surface uses Co-hard 1N-2N gold while a low-touch charm can use soft bright gold

cons.claim: Hardening buys wear at the cost of brittleness and (for Ni) an allergy exposure, so it is not free
cons.example: Ni-hardened gold can fail a nickel-release target from the gold layer itself

failure_modes: forming a hard-gold-plated wire after plating and cracking the deposit
using Ni-hardened gold on a skin-contact SKU sold as hypoallergenic
acceptance_tests: soft (~60-90 HV) vs Co/Ni-hard (~130-200 HV) gold, the 1N-2N/rose/green colour levers, the brittleness form-first rule and the Ni-in-surface catch are stated
revisit_triggers: a colour-match master is re-set
a hard-gold SKU shows bend cracking

nodes.definition: Specify the underplate stack every durable plated finish needs. edges.why_related: nickel is the cheapest, best diffusion barrier but is the common allergen the release limit targets
edges.resolution_rule: use a nickel barrier only where gold/rhodium thickness+porosity keep EN 1811 release below limit after EN 12472; for prolonged skin-contact 18-25 SKUs default to a nickel-free palladium/Pd-Ni barrier and earn the hypoallergenic claim by test

edges.why_related: PVD gives the hardest scratch resistance while vermeil gives the most real gold and a precious-metal base, and both compete for the 'premium finish' slot
edges.resolution_rule: choose PVD/IP when scratch resistance dominates and vermeil when precious-metal content/feel and a defensible 'real gold over sterling' story dominate; never cross-label a PVD finish as vermeil or a nitride-only layer as gold plated

edges.why_related: rhodium's hardness and inertness causally set how a given thickness resists wear and tarnish

conflict_axes.name: thin_gold_plus_topcoat_vs_heavy_bare_gold
conflict_axes.description: A thin gold layer sealed by a topcoat can perform durably and cheaply, but trades away the bare-metal feel and can tempt an inflated finish name versus a heavy bare gold that costs more but is honest in touch and label.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: allow thin+topcoat only when it passes the wear/nickel tests and is labelled by its true gold class; keep bare heavy/hard gold for the real-metal premium tier

conflict_axes.name: nickel_barrier_cost_vs_hypoallergenic_safety
conflict_axes.description: Nickel is the cheapest, best-performing diffusion barrier but is the most common contact allergen the EN 1811 limit targets, so the cheap barrier and the safe barrier diverge for skin-contact wear.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: nickel only where thickness/porosity keep EN 1811 release under limit after wear; default palladium/Pd-Ni for 18-25 skin-contact SKUs and earn the claim by test

conflict_axes.name: rhodium_bright_white_vs_redip_maintenance
conflict_axes.description: Thin rhodium gives the bright bluish-white, tarnish-resistant finish buyers want, but because it is thin and wears it needs periodic re-dip, so the bright finish is not permanent.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: spec a standard 0.1-0.25 um rhodium, disclose the re-dip cycle as normal maintenance, and avoid over-thick brittle builds

conflict_axes.name: pvd_scratch_resistance_vs_electroplate_precious_touch
conflict_axes.description: PVD/IP nitride finishes are the scratch-resistance ceiling but need vacuum capex, resist rework and colour-mismatch electroplate, while electroplated gold gives a true precious-metal surface and easy colour-matching.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: PVD when scratch resistance dominates and a line exists; electroplate for real-gold touch and matched sets; never mix routes in one matched set

conflict_axes.name: honest_ftc_label_vs_marketing_upsell
conflict_axes.description: Marketing wants the most alluring finish name (vermeil, gold plated) while the FTC thresholds may only permit a plainer one (gold flash, rolled gold plate), so allure and legality can pull apart.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: name every finish only by the term whose karat/thickness/base thresholds it meets; upgrade the finish, not the label, when a richer name is wanted

conflict_axes.name: measured_finish_share_vs_fabricated_guess
conflict_axes.description: The owner wants a solid-vs-plated percentage now, but an honest answer is a measured range from an audit, not a confident invented figure.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: encode the storefront-audit + FTC-bucket + rank-weighted method and report a dated range with source; flag any un-audited share as [UNKNOWN]

conflict_axes.name: cost_down_vs_quality_down_value_engineering
conflict_axes.description: Cutting cost by thinning gold or dropping the barrier can look like value engineering but actually lowers quality unless a test-anchored substitute (topcoat, better barrier, wear-zone tuning) holds the durability gate.
poles: cut cost by thinning the stack
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: only cut cost by moves that still pass the SKU's durability tests (topcoat over thin gold, wear-zone-tuned thickness, cheaper base with same finish), never by dropping below the tested gate

conflict_axes.name: hard_gold_scratch_vs_soft_gold_color_ductility
conflict_axes.description: Co/Ni-hardened gold resists scratching on high-wear items but is brittle (cracks if formed after plating) and Ni-hardened risks the allergy limit, while soft gold is bright and ductile but wears fast.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use Co-hardened gold on high-touch wear surfaces with form-first sequencing; use soft gold on low-touch pieces; avoid Ni-hardener where hypoallergenic

conflict_axes.name: rhodium_barrier_vs_leave_silver_antitarnish
conflict_axes.description: A silver piece can be protected either by rhodium plating (bright-white, changes the look) or by leaving the silver bare with a molecular anti-tarnish dip (keeps the silver look but weaker/temporary protection).
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: rhodium when a bright-white durable finish is wanted; anti-tarnish dip when the natural silver colour must show, accepting shorter protection and periodic re-treat

edge_cases.description: Gold-over-brass at 2.5 um is labelled 'vermeil' although vermeil requires a sterling-silver base
edge_cases.trigger: a finish is named vermeil without meeting all three conditions (sterling base, >=10k, >=2.5 um)
edge_cases.mitigation: name it 'gold electroplate' (or 'heavy gold electroplate' if >=2.5 um) and reserve 'vermeil' for the sterling-base build

edge_cases.description: Rhodium flash wears off a white-gold ring shank within months and the warmer alloy shows, read by the customer as a defect
edge_cases.trigger: a thin rhodium layer on a high-touch worn surface with no re-dip disclosure
edge_cases.mitigation: spec standard-class rhodium on wear surfaces and disclose the re-dip cycle up front as normal maintenance

edge_cases.description: A nickel barrier under thin worn gold releases nickel above 0.5 ug/cm2/week after simulated wear, failing EN 1811 on a piece sold as hypoallergenic
edge_cases.trigger: a nickel-barrier skin-contact SKU is claimed hypoallergenic without EN 1811-after-EN 12472 evidence
edge_cases.mitigation: switch to a palladium/Pd-Ni barrier or raise thickness/lower porosity and re-test before making the claim

edge_cases.description: A sterling piece is sold with no rhodium and no anti-tarnish and turns black (Ag2S) in a sulfur-rich environment
edge_cases.trigger: silver exposed to H2S/sulfur (rubber, wool, cosmetics) without a barrier or anti-tarnish film
edge_cases.mitigation: rhodium-plate or apply a molecular anti-tarnish dip and pack with anti-tarnish tissue + desiccant

edge_cases.description: A 0.05 um gold flash is marketed as durable 'gold plated' and wears through to the base in weeks
edge_cases.trigger: a sub-0.175 um flash is named 'gold plated' and put on a wear surface
edge_cases.mitigation: label sub-0.175 um as 'gold flash', reserve it for low-touch pieces, and use plate/micron/heavy classes for wear items

edge_cases.description: A '70% of buyers prefer gold-plated' style statistic is asserted with no audit or source
edge_cases.trigger: a finish-share or preference percentage is stated as measured without the audit method
edge_cases.mitigation: run the storefront-audit method and report a dated range with source, or mark the figure [UNKNOWN]

edge_cases.description: A TiN/ZrN nitride finish with no real gold at the surface is marked 'gold plated'
edge_cases.trigger: a nitride-only PVD colour layer is given a gold-plating marking claim
edge_cases.mitigation: either add a real-gold top flash and mark accordingly or describe it as a gold-tone PVD/IP finish, not gold plated

edge_cases.description: Gold-filled and gold-plated pieces are counted or labelled interchangeably despite ~50-100x difference in gold content and durability
edge_cases.trigger: a category count or label blurs mechanically-bonded gold-filled with thin electroplate
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the two buckets distinct in every count and label; mark gold-filled with karat and fraction

edge_cases.description: Rhodium is specified over-thick (>0.5 um) for 'more durability' and the layer micro-cracks while cost blows up
edge_cases.trigger: a rhodium thickness set well above the standard class on a false 'thicker is better' assumption
edge_cases.mitigation: hold rhodium to ~0.1-0.25 um standard class and get durability from the barrier and disclosed re-dip, not from over-thick rhodium

edge_cases.description: Cost is cut by thinning gold and dropping the barrier, so the piece corrodes at pores even though it is 'cheaper' — a value-engineering failure
edge_cases.trigger: a cost-down move drops the finish below its tested durability gate
edge_cases.mitigation: only cut cost by moves that still pass the durability tests (topcoat over thin gold, wear-zone tuning), never by dropping the barrier or below the tested thickness

edge_cases.description: Base-metal copper migrates through a porous thin gold layer with no barrier and discolours the surface as tarnish-creep
edge_cases.trigger: thin porous gold over copper/brass with no diffusion barrier
edge_cases.mitigation: add a nickel or palladium diffusion barrier and raise thickness to cut porosity below the creep threshold

workflow.action: Fix the FTC frame and purity basis
workflow.description: State 16 CFR Part 23 as the finish-naming frame and the karat/fineness + sterling=925 basis every threshold references
workflow.gate: the FTC frame and the karat/fineness/sterling basis are stated as [FACT]

workflow.action: Establish the tarnish science and rhodium properties
workflow.description: State the Ag + sulfur -> Ag2S reaction and rhodium as a hard, bright-white, inert PGM, correcting the folk model
workflow.gate: the Ag2S mechanism and the four rhodium properties are stated as [FACT]

workflow.description: State gold electroplate/flash, vermeil and gold-filled thresholds precisely with their disqualifiers
workflow.gate: electroplate >=0.175 um, vermeil sterling+>=10k+>=2.5 um, and gold-filled >=1/20 are stated [FACT-FTC]

workflow.action: Compose the rhodium-over-silver and white-gold finish
workflow.description: State rhodium 0.05-0.25 um over sterling/white gold as a dual sulfur-barrier + bright-white finish with re-dip disclosure
workflow.gate: the dual barrier+colour rationale and the re-dip maintenance fact are stated

workflow.action: Design the barrier/strike stack and nickel-release check
workflow.description: Set the strike + nickel-or-palladium diffusion barrier and check EN 1811 for skin-contact SKUs
workflow.gate: the strike, barrier choice, pore/creep mechanism and EN 1811 pivot are stated

workflow.action: Set the gold and rhodium thickness-durability classes
workflow.description: Map flash/plate/micron/heavy gold and flash/standard rhodium to wear zones, with life as an [ESTIMATE]
workflow.gate: the classes, wear ordering and estimate-not-guarantee boundary are stated

workflow.action: Add the topcoat and PVD comparator
workflow.description: Specify e-coat/anti-tarnish topcoat and the PVD/IP hard comparator with their honesty limits
workflow.gate: the pore-sealing/anti-tarnish role, topcoat-last rule and PVD marking rule are stated

workflow.description: Set the adhesion/porosity/tarnish/sweat/wear/XRF/nickel-release battery as the high-quality gate
workflow.gate: the test battery, endpoints and pass-at-wear-zone condition are stated as [FACT-standards]

workflow.description: Build the Pd-barrier + adequate-thickness + compliant-topcoat stack and require EN 1811-after-wear to earn the claim
workflow.gate: the stack and the earned-by-test claim rule are stated

workflow.action: Select and honestly label the finish
workflow.description: Choose the finish by base/wear/tier/safety and bind the FTC-defensible name, rejecting every cross-label
workflow.gate: the finish is chosen and named only by the term whose thresholds it meets

workflow.action: Run the honest finish-share method and route demographics to S1
workflow.description: Encode the storefront-audit + FTC-bucket + rank-weighted [METHOD] and mark any un-audited share [UNKNOWN]
workflow.gate: the method with range-and-source output is stated and no share is invented

workflow.action: Compose the per-SKU finish spec handoff
workflow.gate: the tagged per-SKU finish spec is stated with a clean stop before cost/demand

dominance_rules.rule: The FTC threshold dominates the marketing label
dominance_rules.rationale: 16 CFR Part 23 makes the name a defined term, not an adjective
dominance_rules.trigger: a richer finish name is wanted than the article's karat/thickness/base supports
dominance_rules.action: upgrade the finish to meet the threshold or use the plainer defensible name; never cross-label

dominance_rules.rule: The Ag2S + PGM-barrier science dominates the folk 'shine' model
dominance_rules.rationale: tarnish is a sulfur reaction and rhodium is an inert barrier, not a polish
dominance_rules.trigger: an anti-tarnish or rhodium decision is argued from 'keeps it shiny' rather than the mechanism
dominance_rules.action: reason from the sulfur-barrier mechanism and set thickness/porosity/topcoat accordingly

dominance_rules.rule: Skin-safety compliance dominates the cheapest barrier for 18-25 skin-contact SKUs
dominance_rules.rationale: EN 1811 is a measured legal limit and nickel is the common allergen
dominance_rules.trigger: a nickel barrier is chosen on a prolonged skin-contact piece for cost
dominance_rules.action: default to a nickel-free palladium barrier or prove EN 1811 pass after EN 12472 before shipping

dominance_rules.rule: Sufficient thickness + barrier dominates a thin-flash cost-cut on wear items
dominance_rules.rationale: porosity and wear-through drive pore corrosion and complaints on high-touch pieces
dominance_rules.trigger: flash-class gold is proposed for a ring/bracelet wear surface
dominance_rules.action: use plate/micron/heavy class with a barrier, or a tested thin-gold+topcoat stack

dominance_rules.rule: The honest tag dominates any invented market number
dominance_rules.rationale: finish shares and demographic rates must be measured, never guessed
dominance_rules.trigger: a solid-vs-plated share, demographic or price is about to be stated as fact
dominance_rules.action: replace it with the measurement [METHOD] or an honest [UNKNOWN]

dominance_rules.rule: A passed durability test dominates a durability claim
dominance_rules.rationale: a wear life is an [ESTIMATE] until the acceptance battery measures it
dominance_rules.trigger: a 'lasts N years' or 'high-quality' claim is made without the matching test
dominance_rules.action: downgrade the claim to an [ESTIMATE] or run the test to earn it

dominance_rules.rule: Rhodium re-dip is disclosed maintenance, not a defect
dominance_rules.rationale: thin rhodium wears and the interval is set by thickness and wear pattern
dominance_rules.trigger: rhodium wear-through is treated as a plating failure
dominance_rules.action: disclose the re-dip cycle at sale and offer/plan re-dip rather than scrapping

dominance_rules.rule: Value engineering must hold the tested quality gate
dominance_rules.rationale: cost-down that drops below the durability tests lowers quality, not just price
dominance_rules.trigger: a cost-cut thins gold or removes a barrier
dominance_rules.action: keep only cost moves that still pass the SKU's durability tests; reject those that breach the gate

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the FTC thresholds and defensible name before quoting or marketing a SKU finish
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a relabelling recall when a marketed name fails its karat/thickness/base threshold

anti_rework_rules.rule: Choose the barrier metal (nickel vs palladium) against the EN 1811 target up front
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a full re-plate to reach nickel-release compliance after a hypoallergenic claim is made

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the gold/rhodium thickness class per wear zone before pricing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an underplated wear item that must be re-specced and re-run after wear-through returns

anti_rework_rules.rule: Encode any finish share or demographic figure as a [METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] from the first draft
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retracting a fabricated market statistic the honesty contract forbids

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide topcoat vs bare and form-first vs plate-first before plating
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a strip-and-recoat or a cracked hard-gold deposit from wrong sequencing

anti_rework_rules.rule: Correct the owner's rhodium folk-model once, centrally, into the Ag2S + PGM-barrier science
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the same rhodium misunderstanding resurfacing and misguiding downstream finish and cost decisions

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep gold-filled, vermeil and electroplate as distinct buckets in the glossary before any demand read
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a category miscount that blurs durability and gold content across the finish tiers

anti_rework_rules.rule: Carry the honesty tag ([FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]/[UNKNOWN]) on every claim as it is written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an untested wear life or an invented share propagating unflagged into the cost and assortment chain

iteration_protocol.trigger: the FTC Jewelry Guides (16 CFR Part 23) are amended
iteration_protocol.action: update the finish definitions and the defensible-label logic

iteration_protocol.trigger: EN 1811 / REACH nickel-release limits or methods change, or a new market adds a nickel rule
iteration_protocol.action: update the nickel-release limit and re-derive the skin-safety stack

iteration_protocol.trigger: the rhodium (or palladium) price moves materially
iteration_protocol.action: revisit the rhodium thickness class, re-dip economics and the barrier-metal choice

iteration_protocol.trigger: lab durability results (adhesion/porosity/tarnish/wear/nickel-release) land for a SKU
iteration_protocol.action: retune the thickness classes and convert the wear-life estimate into an evidenced claim

iteration_protocol.trigger: a public data source or storefront audit for finish share is actually run
iteration_protocol.action: populate the finish-share method output with a dated range and source

iteration_protocol.trigger: a poll, assortment or economics specialist requests or flags a finish spec
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the finish selection and the handoff for the affected SKUs

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new topcoat or PVD capability is qualified in the shop
iteration_protocol.action: update the topcoat and PVD comparator and re-open affected finish choices

priority_rationale: The FTC frame, karat/fineness basis, tarnish science and rhodium properties come first because every finish definition, the rhodium-over-silver headline and every honest label depend on those fixed [FACT] anchors; the gold and rhodium finish definitions, colour/hardener, barrier stack and nickel-release limit come next because they are the material building blocks a SKU is assembled from; the thickness-durability classes, topcoat, PVD comparator, skin-safety stack and durability tests then turn those blocks into a wear-rated, compliant, testable finish; and the selection/labelling, honesty ledger, market-share method and finish-spec handoff come last because they compose the compliant SKU spec, keep every number honestly tagged, and hand a clean output to the cost, poll and assortment specialists without overstepping into price or demand.
